mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has risen for two consecutive weeks (-72.0 to -64.6), indicating a recovery momentum in in-person shopping and leisure activity that will persist and continue narrowing the gap to baseline over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC improved from -72.0 at t-2w to -64.6 at t-0w
failure_condition: Mean RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than or equal to the mean over the last 28 days, despite the two-week upward momentum observed in the snapshot.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in RESIDENTIAL time-at-home below a critical threshold signals households resuming out-of-home errands and discretionary trips, which mechanically lifts RETAIL_REC over the following two weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL falls below 18.0 points for two consecutive weekly means
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL declined from 20.0 at t-2w to 17.4 at t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to rise over the next two weeks even though RESIDENTIAL stays below 18.0 points, indicating the threshold does not mechanically translate to retail footfall.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous week-on-week increases in WORKPLACES and TRANSIT indicate restored commuting patterns that generate incidental retail trips near transit hubs and workplaces, compounding to raise RETAIL_REC over four weeks more than either series alone would predict.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES rose from -54.6 to -53.1 and TRANSIT rose from -64.3 to -59.1 over the last two weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC growth over the next four weeks is no greater than the growth predicted by WORKPLACES or TRANSIT individually, indicating no compounding interaction effect.

mechanism_narrative: If local restrictions are in a loosening regime, the concurrent rebound across PARKS, TRANSIT, and WORKPLACES reflects policy-driven reopening that will continue to lift RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks as more venues reopen capacity.
evidence_refs: fact:All three series improved from t-2w to t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC stagnates or declines over the next two weeks despite continued improvement in PARKS, TRANSIT, and WORKPLACES, implying the regime is not actually loosening or policy is not the binding constraint.

mechanism_narrative: Grocery and pharmacy mobility has nearly plateaued (change under 1 point week-on-week at t-0w), suggesting baseline essential-trip demand has stabilized for the late-winter period, which caps further short-term gains in overall retail activity.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM week-on-week change falls below 1.0 point in absolute value
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM changed only from -34.9 to -31.4 week-on-week, a 3.5 point move after a 4.5 point move previously
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC continues to rise over the next week even as GROCERY_PHARM plateaus, indicating essential-trip stabilization does not constrain discretionary retail growth.

mechanism_narrative: After two consecutive weeks of large RETAIL_REC gains (over 5 points per week), pent-up demand becomes exhausted and mean reversion sets in, causing RETAIL_REC growth to decelerate or reverse over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: RETAIL_REC weekly gain exceeds 5 points for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC rose by 1.4 points then 5.7 points over the last two observed weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC continues to rise at a similar or accelerating pace over the next four weeks despite the prior two weeks of strong gains, contradicting the saturation/reversion mechanism.

mechanism_narrative: A strong rebound in PARKS mobility indicates households substituting outdoor recreation for indoor retail and recreation visits, which would suppress RETAIL_REC growth over the next two weeks as time and trip budgets are reallocated to parks.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS improved from -63.7 at t-2w to -58.7 at t-0w, a 5-point gain
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC and PARKS both rise together over the next two weeks, showing no substitution effect between outdoor and retail activity.

mechanism_narrative: The joint pattern of rising TRANSIT and WORKPLACES mobility alongside falling RESIDENTIAL time-at-home signals a coordinated policy-driven reopening that, when all three move together, produces a stronger and more durable lift in RETAIL_REC over four weeks than any single series would predict.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both rise while RESIDENTIAL falls in the same week
evidence_refs: fact:All three series moved in the reopening-consistent direction from t-1w to t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to rise over four weeks even when TRANSIT and WORKPLACES rise and RESIDENTIAL falls simultaneously, indicating no coordinated interaction effect beyond individual series contributions.
